concrete_scene.heading: Worked revision: a lossy ontology migration reaches its consumers
concrete_scene.actor_or_system: A versioned semantic lattice, two parent objects, one retrieval consumer, and an ontology migration
concrete_scene.attempted_action: Migrate both used objects into ontology version 3 while preserving provenance, rights, contradiction state, purpose, and the exact basis recorded by the consumer receipt.
concrete_scene.observable_outcome: Object 1 maps exactly; object 2 is explicitly lossy, records that loss, and invalidates affected consumers instead of allowing a rebuilt index to make the old decision basis look current.
concrete_scene.failed_or_tested_boundary: The scene tests whether storage and retrieval continuity can substitute for semantic compatibility across an ontology change; the lossy mapping blocks that substitution.
concrete_scene.residual_owner: The lattice migration owner retains the unmapped semantic loss, and each invalidated consumer owns re-resolution before reuse.
concrete_scene.evidence_boundary: The dossier and validator check finite authored records only; they establish neither the truth of stored objects nor useful retrieval, complete memory, or deployed forgetting.

worked_trace.heading: Worked revision: a lossy ontology migration reaches its consumers
worked_trace.maximum_inference: The finite review shows how a versioned dossier can preserve history and invalidate a dependent receipt after a lossy mapping; it establishes no semantic truth, retrieval quality, complete memory, behavioral forgetting, or deployment result.

counterexample_or_simpler_baseline: The simpler baseline rebuilds an embedding or graph index and treats successful retrieval as continuity. The chapter requires ontology-loss records and invalidation of every known consumer that used the changed relation.
readable_claim: Durable memory is not a larger context window. It is a revision system that lets a consumer recover which semantic object it used, under which ontology, evidence, time, rights, and contradiction state.
normative_rule: Admit and retrieve memory only through stable object identity, versioned provenance, temporal and rights checks, explicit contradictions, and a use receipt. A correction must invalidate affected consumers without erasing the historical basis of earlier decisions.

formal_binding.anchor: versioned knowledge-lattice contract that binds object and relation identity

caveat_consolidation.local_caveat: The worked migration states once that the object contents and dossier fields are authored rather than observed deployment facts.
caveat_consolidation.consolidated_disposition: Identity, poisoning, ontology, contradiction, privacy, forgetting, learned influence, backup resurrection, and restart limits remain at their mechanism-specific boundaries.

bookkeeping_surface_disposition: The two-object fixture and four receipt-invalidating changes remain in reader prose because they expose the causal mechanism; exhaustive theorem and mutation inventories stay in formal surfaces.

editorial_diagnostics.mega_sentence_disposition: The new projections separate the reader purpose, admission rule, and formal list of lattice obligations.
editorial_diagnostics.hedge_disposition: One local finite-record boundary replaces repeated generic caution while semantic truth, privacy, forgetting, and deployment limits remain distinct.
editorial_diagnostics.table_disposition: No argument-bearing chapter table was removed; status inventories remain confined to the status and evidence sections.

non_claims: The migration fixture does not establish that either stored semantic object is true.
The local review does not establish useful retrieval, complete memory, or behavioral forgetting.
The editorial revision does not move chapter-core support or release state.
